title: GE Aerospace Q3 Earnings Beat Estimates, Guidance Raised Across the Board
excerpt: Adjusted EPS of $2.25 and a 49 percent jump in orders cap a strong quarter for the engine maker.
body:
GE Aerospace delivered a clear third-quarter beat on October 20, 2026, as demand for commercial jet engines and aftermarket services stayed strong. Adjusted earnings per share climbed 36 percent year over year to $2.25, comfortably ahead of the roughly $2.01 consensus estimate. GAAP revenue rose 16 percent to $14.12 billion, while adjusted revenue increased 18 percent to $13.29 billion, also beating expectations.

Orders were the headline number: total orders surged 49 percent to $19.0 billion, pushing the book-to-bill ratio well above one and the commercial services backlog beyond $170 billion. Commercial Engines and Services revenue grew 21 percent to $10.34 billion, driven by services growth of 17 percent and a 38 percent jump in equipment revenue, while the defense business grew about 7 percent. Adjusted operating profit rose 30 percent to about $3.0 billion, with the margin expanding 220 basis points to 22.5 percent.

On the strength of the quarter, GE Aerospace raised its full-year 2026 guidance across every major line: adjusted EPS of $8.00 to $8.10, operating profit of $10.9 billion to $11.0 billion, free cash flow of $9.1 billion to $9.4 billion, and adjusted revenue growth of 19 to 20 percent.

Even so, the stock slipped about 4 percent after the report, as investors focused on a year-over-year dip in quarterly free cash flow and narrower margins in the commercial engines business.
